Nothing in config/ names a D2 for this class: config/arm9/overlays/ov077/symbols.txt holds _ZN7daTgz_cD1Ev and _ZN7daTgz_cD0Ev rows and no third, and rombuild's symbol-home index resolves _ZN7daTgz_cD2Ev to no home at all. With no ROM home there are no cartridge bytes to compare it against, so this is a plain `deadstrip` and NOT a `deadstrip-duplicate`; production isolation discards the body. It is emitted beside the two licensed variants and does not disturb the licensed run.

include/types.h declares Vector3 a deliberately empty inline destructor (`~Vector3() {}`), which makes the type non-POD everywhere, so every TU that gives a Vector3 automatic storage re-emits that destructor as vague linkage. This TU has six such locals: func_ov077_02124d08, func_ov077_021251d0, func_ov077_021253a4, func_ov077_02125550, func_ov077_021256b4 and func_ov077_02125bb4 each declare a block-scope Vector3 that is then passed by reference (dActor_c::SpawnCoins, dActor_c::DetectRaycastClsn, Player::Hurt, Particle::System::New, dBgCh_Gnd::SetObjAndPos). The cartridge keeps exactly one copy at arm9:0x020072c0, kind:function(arm,size=0x4), delinked to src/_ZN7Vector3D1Ev.cpp, which owns it; this object's copy is the identical 4-byte `bx lr` body. rombuild compares it against those cartridge bytes and refuses anything but byte-identical vague-linkage output before the duplicate is discarded, so the address cannot be lost -- the owning source still supplies it.
